```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(AnnoJSON)
```

# Overview

Illumina Connected Annotations (former ica) JSON output is line-oriented:
the first line contains the header and opens the position array, each
subsequent position occupies one line, and an optional top-level gene array
follows the position array. `AnnoJSON` uses this organization to avoid
parsing the complete document as one in-memory JSON object.

The package preserves the output structure used by the aPRoVAR
`read_json.R` workflow. It does not join records, normalize variant keys, or
change row order.

# Read the three raw sections

```{r sections}
example_file <- system.file(
    "extdata",
    "ica-example.json.gz",
    package = "AnnoJSON"
)

parsed_json <- read_ica_sections(
    example_file,
    verbose = FALSE
)

names(parsed_json)
lengths(parsed_json)
```

The result contains one header JSON string, a character vector of position
records, and a character vector of gene records. A file without the
top-level gene section returns `character(0)` for `genes`.

# Parse the records

```{r parse}
header <- parse_ica_header(parsed_json$header)

positions_list <- parse_ica_records(
    parsed_json$positions,
    workers = 1L,
    progress = FALSE
)

genes_list <- parse_ica_records(
    parsed_json$genes,
    workers = 1L,
    progress = FALSE
)
```

For a large local file, set `workers` to the number of independent R
processes that is appropriate for the available memory.

# Create the original aPRoVAR tibbles

```{r tibbles}
tbl_positions <- ica_positions_tibble(positions_list)
tbl_genes <- ica_genes_tibble(genes_list)

tbl_positions
tbl_genes
```

Nested objects remain list-columns. In particular, variant-level annotation
databases such as `gnomad` and `gnomad-exome` are not combined or discarded.

# Run the complete import

```{r one-call}
result <- read_ica_json(
    example_file,
    workers = 1L,
    progress = TRUE,
    verbose = TRUE
)

names(result)
```

# Convert positions to GRanges

```{r granges}
ranges <- ica_positions_granges(result$tbl_positions)
ranges
```

The conversion is an additional representation. It does not modify
`tbl_positions`.

# Convert positions to ICAPositions

```{r ICAPositions}
ICAPositions_object <- ICAPositions(
  positions = parsed_results_master$tbl_positions,
  header = parsed_results_master$header,
  metadata = list(
    source = "ICA JSON",
    package = "AnnoJSON"
  )
)

show(ICAPositions_object)
```

The conversion is an additional representation. It does not modify
`tbl_positions`.
